text: An elephant's ears contain many blood vessels. Flapping them helps transfer heat from circulating blood to the air.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, Asian elephant fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/asian-elephant. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: A fennec fox's oversized ears serve two tasks: shedding heat and locating prey beneath sand.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, fennec fox fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/fennec-fox. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Fennec foxes obtain water from their food and can go for extended periods without drinking.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, fennec fox fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/fennec-fox. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: A beaver's hind foot has a specialized double toenail used to comb its fur, helping preserve insulation and waterproofing.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, beaver fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/beaver. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: A beaver can draw a transparent membrane over its eyes while underwater. Its ears also close during submersion.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, beaver fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/beaver. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Octopuses can rapidly change both skin color and texture under nervous control, transforming the appearance of a soft body.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, giant Pacific octopus research and exhibit report; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/news/smithsonians-national-zoo-gets-new-giant-pacific-octopus. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Aldabra tortoises wallow in mud, which helps protect them from mosquitoes.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, Aldabra tortoise fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/aldabra-tortoise. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Boreal chorus frogs in Yellowstone tolerate freezing while dormant in leaf litter or beneath woody debris during winter.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: National Park Service, Yellowstone amphibians; https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/nature/amphibians.htm. Consulted 2026-10-13.
